blocks.text: The Name Al-Mujeeb The Responsive is found in one place in the Noble Qur'aan. Allaah said,

And to Thamud (people, We sent) their brother Salih (Saleh). He said: "O my people! Worship Allah, you have no other Ilah (God) but Him. He brought you forth from the earth and settled you therein, then ask forgiveness of Him and turn to Him in repentance. Certainly, my Lord is Near (to all by His Knowledge), Responsive."

His Name Al-Mujeeb The Responsive refers to Allaah hearing the supplication of the one who supplicates, answering the request of those who ask and not disappointing a believer when he calls upon Him. He does not reject a plea of a Muslim and He likes that a servant asks Him for all his religious and worldly affairs.

Many ahaadeeth occur in the Prophetic Sunnah encouraging du'aa and they clarify that Allaah is shy and generous. He is the most generous so he will not turn away someone who calls upon Him or disappoint the one who seeks His help or prevent someone who asks of Him.
Aboo Daawood, Tirmidhee and others relate from Salmaan al-Faarisee that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Allaah is The One Possessing Honourable Shame (Hayyiy) and The Generous (Kareem). When a man raises his hands to Him, He feels too shy to return them to him empty and rejected."
blocks.ref: Similar wording in Sunan Aboo Daawood 1488 and Jaami' at-Tirmidhee 3556

blocks.text: In the hadeeth describing the Divine Descent Aboo Hurayrah narrated that Allaah's Messenger ﷺ said,

"Our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, comes down every night to the nearest Heaven to us when the last third of the night remains, saying: 'Is there anyone to invoke Me, so that I may respond to his invocation? Is there anyone to ask Me, so that I may grant him his request? Is there anyone seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?'"

From the effects of the Name Al-Mujeeb upon the faith of a servant is that it strengthens his certainty in Allaah, it increases his hope, it encourages him to turn to Allaah more and hope for what He has (to offer). It also removes despair of Allaah's Mercy or hopelessness regarding His benevolence.

keyPoints: The Name Al-Mujeeb is found in one place in the Noble Qur'aan (Hood 11:61).
Al-Mujeeb refers to Allaah hearing the supplication of the supplicant, answering the request of those who ask and not disappointing a believer who calls upon Him.
He does not reject a Muslim's plea and likes that a servant asks Him for all his religious and worldly affairs.
The Sunnah clarifies that Allaah is shy and generous, too shy to return raised hands empty.
Its effects on the servant: stronger certainty, more hope, turning to Allaah more, and removal of despair of His Mercy.

recall.a: The Responsive: Allaah hears the supplication of the one who supplicates, answers the request of those who ask and does not disappoint a believer who calls upon Him.

recall.q: In which aayah is the Name Al-Mujeeb found?
recall.a: Hood 11:61 – 'Certainly, my Lord is Near (to all by His Knowledge), Responsive.' It is found in one place only.

recall.q: What does Allaah say when He descends in the last third of the night?
recall.a: 'Is there anyone to invoke Me, so that I may respond to his invocation? Is there anyone to ask Me, so that I may grant him his request? Is there anyone seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?'

recall.q: What are the effects of this Name upon the servant's faith?
recall.a: It strengthens his certainty in Allaah, increases his hope, encourages him to turn to Allaah more, and removes despair of Allaah's Mercy.
